chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: The Jazz From a Swinging Era tour and the nine-hour recording
summary: He went overseas with the swing-era all-stars; Earle Warren replaced Willie Smith who died the day before; they recorded an album quickly and talk about tour manager Jack Higgins.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, I went over with this bunch, too. X
Oh yeah. Well, that was quite a tour.
Yes. Lucky that all those guys are still living. Isn't that lucky?
Yeah, that's beautiful. I was just thinking that I know everybody in that band.
Yeah... Willie Smith was supposed to go on that, you know. Earle Warren went in his place, because Willie died. Just the day before we left, he died.
x(This refers to the "Jazz From A Swinging Era" tour.)
There's a record... I guess you have that record you made.
Yeah, I think so. I don't know. I (?).
I remember Rex Vic(?) telling me that that was done...like recorded in nine hours or something, straight through!
Well, we recorded it damn well, I'll tell you that. Then we had to leave right after we recorded it. Going somewhere way down in France; I don't know. Or the ...(?)... Maybe we was going to Milan.
What's the guy's name, the Englishman who ran that tour? Higgins. Jack Higgins.
He's a son-of-a-bitch. He's dead, I think. I don't know... He got fired, I think...
